scenarios.titleEn: Buying a ticket at a rakugo hall
scenarios.titleJa: 寄席でチケットを買う
scenarios.setting: You want to see rakugo for the first time and go to the ticket window of a small variety theater in the evening.
scenarios.partnerRole: the ticket seller at a rakugo hall
goals: Buy one adult ticket
Ask whether you can enter mid-program
Ask if food is allowed
phrases: 大人一枚お願いします。
途中から入ってもいいですか。
中で食べてもいいですか。

turns.partnerJa: いらっしゃいませ。夜の部ですか。
turns.partnerEn: Welcome. For the evening program?
turns.intent: Say yes and ask for one adult ticket.
turns.sample: はい、大人一枚お願いします。

turns.partnerJa: はい、三千円です。もう始まっていますが、よろしいですか。
turns.partnerEn: That's 3,000 yen. It has already started; is that all right?
turns.intent: Ask whether you can go in partway through.
turns.sample: 途中から入ってもいいんですか。

turns.partnerJa: ええ、大丈夫です。噺家が替わるときに、お席へどうぞ。
turns.partnerEn: Yes, that's fine. Please take a seat when the storytellers change over.
turns.intent: Ask whether you can eat or drink inside.
turns.sample: わかりました。中で飲んだり食べたりしてもいいですか。

turns.partnerJa: お弁当や飲み物は大丈夫ですよ。音の出るものだけご遠慮ください。
turns.partnerEn: Bento and drinks are fine. Just please avoid anything noisy.
turns.intent: Thank them and say you'll be careful.
turns.sample: わかりました。気をつけます。ありがとうございます。

scenarios.titleEn: Being offered the seat of honor
scenarios.setting: You're visiting your Japanese friend's grandparents. The grandfather invites you to sit in the seat in front of the tokonoma alcove.
scenarios.partnerRole: the host's grandfather, an older man
goals: Decline the seat of honor once, politely
Accept gracefully when he insists
Compliment the room and the scroll
Ask a question about the house
phrases: いえ、私はこちらで結構です。

turns.partnerJa: さあさあ、どうぞこちらへ。床の間の前にお座りください。
turns.partnerEn: Come, come, this way. Please sit in front of the alcove.
turns.intent: Politely decline the seat of honor once.
turns.sample: いえいえ、私はこちらで結構です。

turns.partnerJa: いやいや、お客さんなんだから、遠慮しないで。
turns.partnerEn: No, no, you're our guest. Don't hold back.
turns.intent: Accept graciously.
turns.sample: では、お言葉に甘えて。失礼します。

turns.partnerJa: 正座じゃなくていいですよ。足を楽にしてください。
turns.partnerEn: You don't have to kneel formally. Make your legs comfortable.
turns.intent: Thank him and say you'll sit formally for a little while first.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。じゃあ、少ししたら崩させていただきます。

turns.partnerJa: この掛け軸はね、私の父が書いたものなんです。
turns.partnerEn: This scroll, you know, my father wrote it.
turns.intent: Compliment the scroll.
turns.sample: そうなんですか。とても力強い字で、素敵な掛け軸ですね。

turns.partnerJa: ありがとう。この家も、もう八十年になるんですよ。
turns.partnerEn: Thank you. This house is eighty years old now.
turns.intent: Show interest and ask about the house.
turns.sample: 八十年ですか。この和室も、そのころのままなんですか。

turns.partnerJa: ええ、畳は何度も替えましたけどね。
turns.partnerEn: Yes, though we've changed the tatami many times.
turns.intent: React and say you like the feel of the room.
turns.sample: そうなんですね。畳の香りがして、とても落ち着きます。

scenarios.titleEn: Renting a kimono for a festival
scenarios.setting: Before a summer festival you visit a kimono rental shop to rent a yukata and have it put on for you.
scenarios.partnerRole: a staff member at a kimono rental shop
goals: Say you'd like to rent a yukata
Choose a pattern and sandals
Ask when to return it
phrases: 浴衣を借りたいんですが。
何時までに返せばいいですか。

turns.partnerJa: いらっしゃいませ。本日はお着物ですか、浴衣ですか。
turns.partnerEn: Welcome. Is it a kimono or a yukata for you today?
turns.intent: Say you'd like to rent a yukata for the festival.
turns.sample: 今晩のお祭りに行くので、浴衣を借りたいんですが。

turns.partnerJa: かしこまりました。こちらからお好きな柄をお選びください。
turns.partnerEn: Certainly. Please choose a pattern you like from these.
turns.intent: Pick the blue one with morning glories.
turns.sample: この青い朝顔の柄にします。

turns.partnerJa: よくお似合いだと思います。履物は下駄と草履、どちらになさいますか。
turns.partnerEn: I think it will suit you well. For footwear, would you like geta or zori?
turns.intent: Choose geta and ask if they are hard to walk in.
turns.sample: 下駄にします。歩きにくくないですか。

turns.partnerJa: 最初は少し慣れないかもしれませんが、鼻緒は柔らかいので大丈夫ですよ。
turns.partnerEn: They may feel strange at first, but the straps are soft, so you'll be fine.
turns.intent: Ask what time you need to return everything.
turns.sample: わかりました。何時までに返せばいいですか。

turns.partnerJa: 夜九時までにお返しください。では、お着付けしますので、こちらへどうぞ。
turns.partnerEn: Please return it by 9 p.m. Now, I'll dress you, so this way please.
turns.intent: Thank her and follow.
turns.sample: 九時ですね。よろしくお願いします。

scenarios.setting: At a neighborhood summer festival, an older woman from the organizing committee waves you over to join the circle of dancers.
scenarios.partnerRole: a friendly older woman on the festival committee
goals: Say you don't know the dance
Ask her to show you the moves
Thank her and say you'll come again next year
phrases: 踊り方がわからないんです。
もう一回見せてもらえますか。

turns.partnerJa: ほら、あなたも一緒に踊りましょうよ！
turns.partnerEn: Come on, dance with us!
turns.intent: Say you'd like to but don't know how.
turns.sample: 踊りたいんですけど、踊り方がわからないんです。

turns.partnerJa: 大丈夫、大丈夫。前の人のまねをすればいいのよ。
turns.partnerEn: It's okay. Just copy the person in front of you.
turns.intent: Say okay and join in.
turns.sample: じゃあ、やってみます。

turns.partnerJa: 手を上に、パン、パンと二回たたいて、右に一歩。
turns.partnerEn: Hands up, clap-clap twice, and one step to the right.
turns.intent: Ask her to show you once more.
turns.sample: すみません、もう一回見せてもらえますか。

turns.partnerJa: はい、手を上に、パン、パン、右に一歩。そうそう、上手！
turns.partnerEn: Okay: hands up, clap, clap, one step right. That's it, great!
turns.intent: Say it's fun and the drums are great.
turns.sample: 楽しいですね！太鼓の音もかっこいいです。

turns.partnerJa: でしょう？この町の盆踊りは五十年続いてるのよ。
turns.partnerEn: Right? This town's bon dance has been going for fifty years.
turns.intent: React with surprise.
turns.sample: 五十年ですか！すごいですね。

turns.partnerJa: 来年は浴衣で来てね。
turns.partnerEn: Come in a yukata next year.
turns.intent: Thank her and say you'll come again next year.
turns.sample: はい、来年は浴衣で来ます。ありがとうございました。

turns.partnerJa: こちらこそ。気をつけて帰ってね。
turns.partnerEn: Thank you too. Get home safe.
turns.intent: Say goodbye politely.
turns.sample: はい、おやすみなさい。

scenarios.titleEn: Giving the opening toast at a farewell party
scenarios.titleJa: 送別会で乾杯の音頭をとる
scenarios.setting: Your department is holding a farewell party at a restaurant for Ms. Endo, who is transferring. The organizer asks you, as her junior, to lead the toast.
scenarios.learnerRole: a junior colleague asked to lead the toast
scenarios.partnerRole: the party organizer, a senior colleague
goals: Accept the role modestly
Give a short speech of thanks to the departing colleague
Lead the toast with the right formula
Thank everyone and hand the floor back
phrases: 僭越ながら、乾杯の音頭をとらせていただきます。
大変お世話になりました。
ご健康とご活躍を祈って、乾杯！

turns.partnerJa: では、ここで乾杯の音頭を、遠藤さんのチームのジョンさんにお願いします。
turns.partnerEn: Now, for the toast, we'll ask John from Ms. Endo's team.
turns.intent: Stand, and modestly accept the role.
turns.sample: ご指名いただきましたので、僭越ながら乾杯の音頭をとらせていただきます。

turns.partnerJa: 皆さん、グラスをお持ちください。
turns.partnerEn: Everyone, please pick up your glasses.
turns.intent: Mention how long you have worked with Ms. Endo.
turns.sample: 遠藤さんには、入社してから二年間、本当にお世話になりました。

turns.partnerJa: （皆がうなずく）
turns.partnerEn: (Everyone nods.)
turns.intent: Give one concrete memory of her help.
turns.sample: 初めてのプレゼンのとき、夜遅くまで練習に付き合ってくださったことは、一生忘れません。

turns.partnerJa: （遠藤さんが照れて笑う）
turns.partnerEn: (Ms. Endo smiles, embarrassed.)
turns.intent: Say she will be missed and wish her well in her new post.
turns.sample: 遠藤さんがいなくなるのは寂しいですが、新しい職場でのご活躍を心から願っております。

turns.partnerJa: （皆、グラスを持ち上げる）
turns.partnerEn: (Everyone raises their glass.)
turns.intent: Lead the toast.
turns.sample: それでは、遠藤さんのご健康とますますのご活躍を祈って、乾杯！

turns.partnerJa: 乾杯！
turns.partnerEn: Cheers!
turns.intent: Thank everyone and hand the floor back to the organizer.
turns.sample: ありがとうございました。どうぞ、ごゆっくりお楽しみください。

turns.partnerJa: ジョンさん、素晴らしいスピーチでした。
turns.partnerEn: John, that was a wonderful speech.
turns.intent: Respond modestly.
turns.sample: いえいえ、緊張してしまって、お恥ずかしいです。

turns.partnerJa: 遠藤さんも喜んでいましたよ。
turns.partnerEn: Ms. Endo was delighted too.
turns.intent: Say you're glad and you'll go pour a drink for her.
turns.sample: それならよかったです。あとで遠藤さんにお酌をしに行ってきます。

scenarios.titleEn: New Year visit to a friend's family
scenarios.titleJa: 友人の実家への年始の挨拶
scenarios.setting: On January 2 you visit your friend Haruka's family home. Her father opens the door.
scenarios.learnerRole: a guest visiting for the New Year
goals: Give the New Year greeting correctly
Present a gift modestly
Accept food and drink politely
Answer questions about your life in Japan
Take your leave with the right phrases
phrases: 明けましておめでとうございます。
今年もよろしくお願いします。
つまらないものですが。

turns.partnerJa: やあ、いらっしゃい。遥香から話は聞いていますよ。
turns.partnerEn: Hello, welcome. Haruka has told us about you.
turns.intent: Give the New Year greeting and introduce yourself.
turns.sample: 明けましておめでとうございます。遥香さんの友人のリサです。今年もよろしくお願いします。

turns.partnerJa: おめでとうございます。さあ、上がってください。
turns.partnerEn: Happy New Year to you. Come on in.
turns.intent: Say the phrase for entering a home.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。お邪魔します。

turns.partnerJa: 寒かったでしょう。こたつに入ってくださいね。
turns.partnerEn: It must have been cold. Please get into the kotatsu.
turns.intent: Thank him and present your gift modestly.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。あの、これ、つまらないものですが、皆さんでどうぞ。

turns.partnerJa: これはご丁寧に。お、おいしそうなお菓子だ。
turns.partnerEn: How kind of you. Oh, these sweets look delicious.
turns.intent: Say it's a specialty from your hometown.
turns.sample: 私の国のお菓子なんです。お口に合うといいんですが。

turns.partnerJa: おせち料理もありますから、たくさん食べてください。
turns.partnerEn: There's New Year food too, so please eat plenty.
turns.intent: Accept and say the phrase before eating.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。では、いただきます。

turns.partnerJa: 日本の生活はどうですか。もう慣れましたか。
turns.partnerEn: How is life in Japan? Are you used to it now?
turns.intent: Say you are getting used to it, thanks to Haruka.
turns.sample: はい、おかげさまで、だいぶ慣れました。遥香さんにいつも助けてもらっています。

turns.partnerJa: それはよかった。お正月はどこかへ行きましたか。
turns.partnerEn: Good to hear. Did you go anywhere over New Year?
turns.intent: Say you went on a first shrine visit on New Year's Day.
turns.sample: 元日に、近くの神社に初詣に行きました。

turns.partnerJa: おみくじは引きましたか。
turns.partnerEn: Did you draw a fortune?
turns.intent: Say you got 大吉 (great luck).
turns.sample: はい、大吉でした！

turns.partnerJa: それは縁起がいい。今年はいい年になりますね。
turns.partnerEn: That's a good omen. It'll be a good year for you.
turns.intent: Say it is getting late and you should go.
turns.sample: ありがとうございます。そろそろ失礼します。ご馳走様でした。

turns.partnerJa: また遊びに来てくださいね。
turns.partnerEn: Please come visit again.
turns.intent: Thank him and say goodbye at the door.
turns.sample: 今日は本当にありがとうございました。失礼します。

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ジャック君、玄関で靴を脱いだら、このスリッパを履いてね。
lines.en: Jack, after you take off your shoes in the genkan, put on these slippers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。靴はこのままでいいですか。
lines.en: Okay. Can I leave my shoes like this?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: つま先をドアの方に向けて、端に置いておくといいよ。
lines.en: It's good to turn the toes toward the door and put them at the side.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。スリッパで和室に入ってもいいですか。
lines.en: Got it. Can I go into the tatami room in slippers?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ううん、畳の上ではスリッパを脱ぐの。
lines.en: No, you take slippers off on the tatami.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですね。トイレにも別のスリッパがありますね。
lines.en: I see. There are separate slippers for the toilet too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そう。トイレのスリッパで廊下を歩かないでね。
lines.en: Right. Don't walk in the hall with the toilet slippers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 気をつけます。覚えることがたくさんありますね。
lines.en: I'll be careful. There's a lot to remember.

questions.question: Where should Jack NOT wear the regular slippers?
Which way should his shoes point?

dialogues.title: Choosing a gift for a client visit

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 明日の訪問だけど、手土産はもう用意した？
lines.en: About tomorrow's visit, have you got the gift ready?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: まだです。何がいいでしょうか。
lines.en: Not yet. What would be good?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 先方は社員が二十人くらいだから、個包装のお菓子がいいね。
lines.en: They have about twenty staff, so individually wrapped sweets would be good.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。皆さんで分けやすいですね。
lines.en: I see. Easy for everyone to share.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それと、相手の会社の近くで買うのはやめたほうがいい。
lines.en: Also, better not to buy it near their office.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: どうしてですか。
lines.en: Why is that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 急いで買ったように見えるからね。こちらの地元のものが喜ばれるよ。
lines.en: It looks like you bought it in a hurry. Something from our own area is appreciated.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。渡すときは「つまらない物ですが」でいいですか。
lines.en: Understood. When I hand it over, is 'it's only a trifle' okay?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 最近は「心ばかりですが」や「皆様で召し上がってください」も多いよ。
lines.en: These days people often say 'a small token' or 'please enjoy it together' too.

questions.question: Why should Ryan avoid buying the gift near the client's office?
choices: It looks like a last-minute purchase

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 昨日、初めて寄席に行ったんだ。
lines.en: Yesterday I went to a rakugo hall for the first time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: へえ、落語ってどんな感じ？
lines.en: Oh, what's rakugo like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 噺家が一人で高座に座って、いろいろな人の役を演じるの。
lines.en: One storyteller sits on the stage and plays all sorts of characters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 一人で？道具は使わないの？
lines.en: Alone? No props?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 扇子と手拭いだけ。扇子がお箸になったり、手拭いが財布になったりするんだよ。
lines.en: Just a fan and a hand towel. The fan becomes chopsticks, the towel becomes a wallet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 面白いね。そばを食べるところとか？
lines.en: Fun. Like eating soba?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そう！音が本物みたいで、客席がみんな笑ってた。
lines.en: Yes! The sound was so real the whole audience laughed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 今度、一緒に行きたいな。
lines.en: I'd like to go with you next time.

questions.question: What props does a rakugo storyteller use?
choices: A fan and a hand towel

dialogues.title: Planning the seating for a client dinner

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 来週の会食、座敷の個室を予約しておきました。
lines.en: I've booked a private tatami room for next week's dinner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。席順はどうしましょうか。
lines.en: Thank you. How shall we arrange the seats?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 床の間の前が上座なので、先方の社長にはそこに座っていただきます。
lines.en: The seat in front of the alcove is the seat of honor, so their president will sit there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 私たちは入り口側ですね。
lines.en: We'll be on the door side, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ええ。一番下座には私が座ります。注文や店員さんとのやりとりがありますから。
lines.en: Yes. I'll take the lowest seat, since I'll handle the orders and talk to the staff.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 部長はどこに座っていただけばいいですか。
lines.en: Where should our director sit?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 社長の向かいにお願いしましょう。お二人で話しやすいように。
lines.en: Let's have him opposite their president, so the two can talk easily.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。当日は私が玄関でお出迎えします。
lines.en: Understood. On the day, I'll greet them at the entrance.

questions.question: Why will Sato take the lowest seat?
choices: She will handle orders and the staff

questions.question: Where will the client's president sit?

dialogues.title: The portable shrine at the festival

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おじいちゃん、あの大きくて金色のもの、何？
lines.en: Grandpa, what's that big golden thing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あれは神輿だよ。神様が乗っているんだ。
lines.en: That's a mikoshi. A god rides in it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: みんなで担いで、どこへ行くの？
lines.en: Where are they carrying it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 町の中を回って、夕方に神社へ帰るんだよ。
lines.en: Around the town, and back to the shrine in the evening.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 太鼓の音、大きいね！
lines.en: The drums are so loud!

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: おじいちゃんも若いころは、毎年担いでいたんだよ。
lines.en: When I was young, I carried it every year too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すごい！ぼくも大きくなったら担ぎたい。
lines.en: Wow! I want to carry it when I grow up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: じゃあ、まず子ども神輿から始めようか。
lines.en: Then let's start with the children's mikoshi.

questions.question: Where does the mikoshi go in the evening?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 初めての能は、どうでしたか。
lines.en: How was your first noh play?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: とても静かで、不思議な舞台でした。
lines.en: It was a very quiet, mysterious stage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 能面をつけると、角度で表情が変わって見えるんですよ。
lines.en: With a noh mask, the expression seems to change with the angle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 本当に、下を向くと悲しそうに見えました。
lines.en: Really, when he looked down, it looked sad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 間に狂言もありましたね。
lines.en: There was a kyogen piece in between, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、狂言は言葉がわかりやすくて、観客もよく笑っていました。
lines.en: Yes, kyogen was easier to understand, and the audience laughed a lot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 能と狂言は、昔から一緒に演じられてきたんです。
lines.en: Noh and kyogen have been performed together since long ago.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですか。次は解説を読んでから見に来たいです。
lines.en: Really? Next time I want to read the explanation before coming.

questions.question: According to Clara, what did kyogen feel like compared with noh?
What happens when the actor tilts the mask downward?

drills.title: Visiting a friend's home
drills.setting: You arrive at the Morimoto family's house for dinner. Mrs. Morimoto opens the door and you stand in the genkan.
staging: Say お邪魔します before stepping up from the genkan; step up facing forward, then kneel and turn your shoes to point at the door, set to one side.
Slippers go on in the hallway but come off before tatami; never wear them onto the mats.
Call the host 森本さん (or 奥さん only if she is clearly the host's wife); never attach さん to your own name.
For a casual visit the gift can be handed over in the genkan; for a formal visit wait until you are seated in the room. Take it out of its shop bag and present it with both hands, front facing her.
The host downplays trouble (気を遣わなくても); you insist lightly once, not repeatedly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いらっしゃい。どうぞ、上がってください。
lines.en: Welcome. Please come in.
lines.stage: Host opens the door and gives a small bow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お邪魔します。
lines.en: Excuse me for intruding.
lines.stage: Small bow (about 15 degrees) while still standing on the genkan floor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 遠いところ、ありがとうございます。スリッパをどうぞ。
lines.en: Thank you for coming all this way. Here are some slippers.
lines.stage: She sets slippers on the step, toes pointing inward.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。あの、これ、つまらないものですが、どうぞ。
lines.en: Thank you. Um, this is just a small thing, but please.
lines.stage: Take the gift out of its bag and hold it out with both hands, front facing her.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: まあ、ご丁寧に。気を遣わなくてもよかったのに。
lines.en: Oh, how kind. You didn't have to go to the trouble.
lines.stage: She receives it with both hands and a small bow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いえいえ。皆さんで召し上がってください。
lines.en: Not at all. Please enjoy it with everyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、遠慮なくいただきます。どうぞ、こちらの部屋へ。
lines.en: Then I'll gladly accept. Please, this way to the room.
lines.stage: She slides open the fusuma to the tatami room.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 失礼します。
lines.en: Excuse me.
lines.stage: Step out of the slippers, leave them neatly at the edge, and enter in socks.

drills.title: Visiting a teacher's office
drills.titleJa: 先生の研究室を訪ねる
drills.setting: You knock on Professor Tamura's office door to ask for help with a speech contest manuscript.
staging: 先生 is already a title: say 田村先生, never 田村先生さん, and never call yourself 先生.
Knock twice, wait for どうぞ, then enter with 失礼します and a small bow at the doorway.
Stay standing until the teacher tells you to sit.
Leave with 失礼しました (past tense: the visit is over) and a 30-degree bow before closing the door quietly.
The teacher may speak plainly and call you エマさん; you stay in です/ます and ask with 〜ていただけませんか.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 失礼します。田村先生、今よろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: Excuse me. Professor Tamura, do you have a moment?
lines.stage: Knock twice, wait for a reply, open the door, bow slightly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ああ、エマさん。どうぞ、入ってください。
lines.en: Ah, Emma. Please, come in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 来週のスピーチ大会のことで、ご相談があります。
lines.en: I'd like to consult you about next week's speech contest.
lines.stage: Stand near the desk; don't sit yet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いいですよ。そこに座ってください。
lines.en: Sure. Have a seat there.
lines.stage: He gestures to a chair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。原稿を見ていただけませんか。
lines.en: Thank you. Would you look over my manuscript?
lines.stage: Hand it over with both hands, text facing the teacher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。明日までに読んでおきます。
lines.en: All right. I'll read it by tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お忙しいところ、ありがとうございました。
lines.en: Thank you for your time when you're so busy.
lines.stage: Stand up and bow about 30 degrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いいえ。頑張ってくださいね。
lines.en: Not at all. Good luck.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。失礼しました。
lines.en: I will. Excuse me.
lines.stage: Bow again at the door, then close it quietly.

drills.title: Exchanging business cards
drills.setting: At a first meeting with a client company, you and section manager Ishikawa exchange business cards before sitting down.
staging: Stand for the exchange; hold your card with both hands at chest height, your name facing the other person.
Name your own company and your own family name with no honorific (青葉商事のスミスと申します); refer to their company as 御社.
Offer your card slightly lower than theirs to show deference; when both give at once, give with the right hand and receive with the left, then support with both.
Say 頂戴いたします as you receive. Never pocket the card or write on it in front of them: lay it on your card case on the table for the whole meeting.
In speech call him 石川さん or 石川課長; 石川様 is for letters and email.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 初めまして。青葉商事のスミスと申します。
lines.en: How do you do. I'm Smith from Aoba Trading.
lines.stage: Hold your card in both hands, name facing him, at chest height.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 初めまして。北星工業の石川と申します。
lines.en: How do you do. I'm Ishikawa from Hokusei Industries.
lines.stage: He holds out his card the same way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。
lines.en: I look forward to working with you.
lines.stage: Offer your card slightly lower than his and bow about 30 degrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 頂戴いたします。こちらこそ、よろしくお願いいたします。
lines.en: Thank you. The pleasure is mine.
lines.stage: Simultaneous exchange: give with the right hand, receive with the left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 頂戴いたします。恐れ入りますが、お名前は何とお読みすればよろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: Thank you. Excuse me, but how should I read your given name?
lines.stage: Look at the card with both hands; keep it above waist level.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 「しげる」と読みます。よく聞かれるんですよ。
lines.en: It's read Shigeru. People often ask.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you. And thank you for making time for us today.
lines.stage: Place his card on top of your card case on the table.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いえいえ。どうぞおかけください。
lines.en: Not at all. Please have a seat.
lines.stage: He motions toward the chairs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 失礼いたします。
lines.en: Thank you (excuse me).
lines.stage: Sit only after he sits or after being invited, in the seat you are shown.

drills.title: Checking in at a ryokan
drills.setting: You arrive at a hot-spring inn. The proprietress greets you from the raised floor of the entrance.
staging: The okami kneels and bows deeply; answer with a polite bow of your own, standing is fine.
Take off your shoes in the genkan and leave them: staff put them away and bring them out when you leave.
Staff call you リー様 and speak full 敬語; you can answer in simple です/ます without matching their keigo.
In the room, sit on the zabuton, not beside it; never step on or over other people's cushions.
Wrap the yukata left side over right; right over left is how the deceased are dressed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いらっしゃいませ。遠いところをようこそお越しくださいました。
lines.en: Welcome. Thank you for coming all this way.
lines.stage: She kneels on the raised floor and bows deeply.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: こんにちは。今夜予約しているリーです。
lines.en: Hello. I'm Lee, I have a reservation for tonight.
lines.stage: Bow in return, then step out of your shoes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: リー様でございますね。お待ちしておりました。お部屋へご案内いたします。
lines.en: Mr. Lee. We have been expecting you. I will show you to your room.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お願いします。
lines.en: Thank you.
lines.stage: Leave your shoes; follow her down the corridor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: こちらが椿の間でございます。お茶をお入れいたしますので、どうぞおくつろぎください。
lines.en: This is the Camellia Room. I will make you some tea, so please relax.
lines.stage: Sit on the zabuton at the low table.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。夕食は何時からですか。
lines.en: Thank you. What time is dinner?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 六時半から、こちらのお部屋にお持ちいたします。お風呂は十一時までご利用いただけます。
lines.en: We will bring it to this room from six thirty. The bath is open until eleven.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。浴衣はこれを着ればいいですか。
lines.en: I see. Should I wear this yukata?
lines.stage: Point to the folded yukata.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。左の前を上にしてお召しください。
lines.en: Yes. Please wear it with the left side on top.
lines.stage: She demonstrates with her hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 左が上ですね。気をつけます。
lines.en: Left on top. I'll be careful.
lines.stage: Small nod of thanks.

drills.title: A toast at the izakaya
drills.setting: After work you and your senior colleague Yamaguchi sit down at an izakaya. As the junior, you do the ordering.
staging: Ordering for the table and calling the server (すみません！) is the junior's job.
Nobody drinks before 乾杯; wait until every glass has arrived.
When glasses touch, keep your rim lower than your senior's.
Pour for others, never for yourself, and watch your senior's glass; hold the bottle with both hands.
The senior talks casually (お疲れ様、食べてね); the junior stays in です/ます (お疲れ様です).

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 何飲む？とりあえず生でいい？
lines.en: What'll you drink? Draft beer to start?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。すみません！生二つと枝豆、お願いします。
lines.en: Yes. Excuse me! Two draft beers and edamame, please.
lines.stage: Raise a hand and call toward the counter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 焼き鳥も頼もうか。
lines.en: Shall we get yakitori too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうですね。すみません、焼き鳥の盛り合わせも追加でお願いします。
lines.en: Good idea. Excuse me, could we add a yakitori platter too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: よし、来たね。じゃあ、今週もお疲れ様。乾杯！
lines.en: Right, they're here. Well, good work this week. Cheers!
lines.stage: Raise glasses; wait for his lead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 乾杯！お疲れ様です。
lines.en: Cheers! Good work.
lines.stage: Touch glasses with your rim lower than his.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 遠慮しないで、どんどん食べてね。
lines.en: Don't hold back, eat up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。いただきます。先輩、お注ぎしましょうか。
lines.en: Thank you. Let's eat. Shall I pour for you?
lines.stage: Put hands together briefly; later, pour with both hands on the bottle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お、ありがとう。気が利くね。
lines.en: Oh, thanks. Very thoughtful.
lines.stage: He holds his glass up with one hand under it.

drills.title: Receiving a souvenir
drills.setting: Your neighbor Mrs. Sasaki has just come back from a trip and stops by your door with a small box of sweets.
staging: Receive with both hands and a small bow; one light protest (いいんですか) is natural, more is awkward.
Ask before opening a gift in front of the giver.
The giver downplays the gift (大したものじゃない); the receiver warmly upgrades it (とても嬉しい).
Travel souvenirs need no return gift; for celebrations a return gift (お返し) of about half the value is customary.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: これ、旅行のお土産なんですけど、よかったらどうぞ。
lines.en: This is a souvenir from my trip. Please take it if you like.
lines.stage: She holds the box out with both hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: えっ、いいんですか。わざわざありがとうございます。
lines.en: Oh, are you sure? Thank you for thinking of me.
lines.stage: Receive it with both hands and bow slightly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 大したものじゃないんですけど。
lines.en: It's nothing special.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いえ、とても嬉しいです。開けてもいいですか。
lines.en: No, I'm really happy. May I open it?
lines.stage: Glance up at her before touching the wrapping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: どうぞどうぞ。
lines.en: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わあ、きれいなお菓子ですね。家族でいただきます。
lines.en: Wow, what beautiful sweets. We'll enjoy them as a family.
lines.stage: Open carefully, without tearing the paper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 喜んでもらえてよかった。
lines.en: I'm glad you like them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 今度、旅行のお話を聞かせてください。
lines.en: Please tell me about your trip sometime.
lines.stage: Small bow as she turns to leave.

drills.title: Apologizing to a neighbor
drills.setting: Your friends stayed late last night and were noisy. The next day you visit the neighbor next door, Mr. Yamashita, to apologize.
staging: Apologize in person and soon; a deeper, longer bow (about 45 degrees, held for two seconds) shows a sincere apology.
Apology first, a brief reason second, a promise last; don't open with excuses.
Use 申し訳ありませんでした rather than すみません for a real apology to an older neighbor.
A small, inexpensive gift such as sweets softens the apology; hand it over with both hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ごめんください。隣の302号室の者です。
lines.en: Hello, excuse me. I'm from room 302 next door.
lines.stage: Ring the bell and step back a little from the door.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、何でしょう。
lines.en: Yes, what is it?
lines.stage: He opens the door halfway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 昨夜は遅くまでうるさくして、本当に申し訳ありませんでした。
lines.en: I'm truly sorry for being so noisy until late last night.
lines.stage: Deep bow, about 45 degrees; hold it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ああ、ちょっと声が響いていましたね。
lines.en: Ah, yes, your voices were carrying a bit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 友達が来ていて、つい話し込んでしまいました。これから気をつけます。
lines.en: Friends were over and we got carried away talking. I'll be careful from now on.
lines.stage: Keep your eyes lowered; speak calmly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。次から気をつけてくれれば大丈夫ですよ。
lines.en: All right. As long as you're careful next time, it's fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。これ、ほんの気持ちですが。
lines.en: Thank you. This is just a small token.
lines.stage: Offer a box of sweets with both hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そんな、気を遣わなくていいのに。じゃあ、いただきます。
lines.en: Oh, you didn't need to. Well, thank you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 本当にご迷惑をおかけしました。失礼します。
lines.en: I'm sorry for the trouble. Goodbye.
lines.stage: Bow again before he closes the door.

drills.title: Visiting a shrine
drills.setting: A local volunteer guide, Mrs. Nakajima, walks you through visiting a neighborhood shrine for the first time.
staging: Bow lightly once before passing under the torii, and again when leaving.
Walk at the side of the approach; the center is said to be the path of the deity.
At the water basin: rinse the left hand, the right hand, pour water into the left palm to rinse the mouth, then tip the ladle upright so the water runs down the handle.
At the hall: gently drop the offering in, ring the bell, then two bows, two claps, one bow. Temples differ: no clapping there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 鳥居をくぐる前に、軽くお辞儀をしましょう。
lines.en: Let's bow lightly before we pass through the torii.
lines.stage: Stop in front of the torii; both bow about 15 degrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。真ん中は通らないほうがいいんですよね。
lines.en: Okay. It's better not to walk down the middle, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうです。真ん中は神様の通り道ですから、端を歩きます。
lines.en: That's right. The middle is the deity's path, so we walk at the side.
lines.stage: Move to the edge of the path.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 手水舎では、まず左手を洗うんですか。
lines.en: At the water basin, do I wash my left hand first?
lines.stage: Take the ladle in your right hand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ええ。左手、右手、それから口をすすいで、最後にひしゃくを立てて柄を洗います。
lines.en: Yes. Left hand, right hand, then rinse your mouth, and finally stand the ladle up to rinse the handle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お賽銭を入れて、鈴を鳴らして……次は？
lines.en: I put in the offering, ring the bell... and then?
lines.stage: Drop the coin in gently; don't throw it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 二回お辞儀、二回拍手、最後にもう一回お辞儀です。
lines.en: Bow twice, clap twice, then one last bow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 二礼二拍手一礼ですね。やってみます。
lines.en: Two bows, two claps, one bow. I'll try.
lines.stage: Deep bows (about 90 degrees), claps at chest height, a silent wish, final bow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 上手ですよ。おみくじも引いてみますか。
lines.en: Well done. Would you like to draw a fortune too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、ぜひ！
lines.en: Yes, definitely!

drills.title: A guest at a tea gathering
drills.setting: At a small tea gathering, you sit as a guest. The host, Ms. Matsui, serves sweets and then a bowl of matcha.
staging: Before taking sweets or tea, bow to the guest after you and say お先に; before drinking, bow to the host with お点前頂戴いたします.
Bows here are seated bows: hands on the tatami in front of your knees.
Turn the bowl about a quarter turn twice clockwise so you don't drink from its front; turn it back before returning it.
Admire the bowl low, elbows on your knees, close to the tatami, never lifting it high.
Everything is 敬語; the host humbles herself (恐れ入ります), and the guest praises (結構なお点前でございました).

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: どうぞ、お菓子をお取りください。
lines.en: Please help yourself to a sweet.
lines.stage: She sets the sweets tray down and bows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お先に頂戴いたします。
lines.en: Excuse me for going first.
lines.stage: Bow slightly to the guest on your left, then place a sweet on your paper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: どうぞ、お召し上がりください。
lines.en: Please, have some tea.
lines.stage: She sets the bowl down with its front facing you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お点前頂戴いたします。
lines.en: I gratefully receive your tea.
lines.stage: Bow to the host, hands on the tatami; turn the bowl twice clockwise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お服加減はいかがでございますか。
lines.en: How is the tea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 大変結構でございます。
lines.en: It is excellent.
lines.stage: Finish in a few sips; the last one may make a soft sound.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 結構なお点前でございました。
lines.en: Thank you for the lovely tea.
lines.stage: Wipe the rim with your fingers, turn the bowl back, and return it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 恐れ入ります。
lines.en: You are too kind.
lines.stage: She bows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: こちらのお茶碗は、どちらの窯のものでございますか。
lines.en: May I ask which kiln this bowl comes from?
lines.stage: Look at the bowl low over the tatami.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 京都の小さな窯のもので、祖母から受け継いだものでございます。
lines.en: It is from a small kiln in Kyoto; I inherited it from my grandmother.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 趣のある、素晴らしいお茶碗でございますね。
lines.en: What a beautiful bowl, full of character.
lines.stage: Place it back with its front toward the host.

drills.title: Finding your seat at the kabuki theater
drills.setting: At a kabuki theater, you show your ticket to an usher and ask a few questions before the curtain rises.
staging: Ushers speak formal keigo (〜でございます、ご遠慮いただいております); a 'no' is phrased softly.
Reply to guidance with a quick 会釈 (about 15 degrees); no deep bow needed.
Eat your bento in your seat only during the intermission (幕間), never during the play.
Shouts from the audience are left to experienced regulars; ordinary guests clap, especially at a 見得.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、この席はどこでしょうか。
lines.en: Excuse me, where is this seat?
lines.stage: Show the ticket with both hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 拝見いたします。一階の十列、十五番でございますね。花道の近くのお席です。ご案内いたします。
lines.en: May I see? Ground floor, row ten, seat fifteen. It's near the runway. I'll show you.
lines.stage: She gestures with an open hand, fingers together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。幕間は何分ありますか。
lines.en: Thank you. How long is the intermission?
lines.stage: Follow her; a small nod when she stops at the row.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 一回目の幕間は三十分でございます。お弁当はお席でお召し上がりいただけます。
lines.en: The first intermission is thirty minutes. You may eat your bento in your seat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 上演中に写真を撮ってもいいですか。
lines.en: May I take photos during the performance?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 申し訳ございません、上演中の撮影はご遠慮いただいております。
lines.en: I'm sorry, but we ask that you refrain from photography during the performance.
lines.stage: A small apologetic bow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。それから、掛け声は客席からかけてもいいんですか。
lines.en: I see. Also, can people in the audience shout out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 掛け声は慣れた方がかけるものですので、お客様は拍手でお楽しみください。
lines.en: Shout-outs are done by experienced regulars, so please enjoy by clapping.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。ありがとうございました。
lines.en: I see. Thank you very much.
lines.stage: Quick 会釈 before sitting down.

drills.title: Greeting at a wedding reception
drills.setting: At your friend Yumi's wedding reception, her mother comes over to greet you after you have handed your gift money at the reception desk.
staging: Carry the ご祝儀 envelope in a fukusa; unwrap it at the reception desk and hand it over with the writing facing the receiver.
Avoid 忌み言葉 such as 切れる、別れる、終わる and repeated words like 重ね重ね.
Call the bride's mother お母様 and the bride 由美さん; formal keigo is expected at the start, a warmer tone once she relaxes.
Bow about 30 degrees with hands together in front; keep congratulations short, since she has many guests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: まあ、アンナさん。今日は遠いところ、来てくださってありがとうございます。
lines.en: Oh, Anna. Thank you for coming all this way today.
lines.stage: She approaches your table; stand up to greet her.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 本日は誠におめでとうございます。お招きいただき、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Heartfelt congratulations on this day. Thank you for inviting me.
lines.stage: Bow about 30 degrees, hands together in front.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 由美も、アンナさんが来るのをとても楽しみにしていたんですよ。
lines.en: Yumi was really looking forward to you coming.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 私もです。由美さん、とてもおきれいでした。
lines.en: So was I. Yumi looked so beautiful.
lines.stage: Smile; this part can be warmer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。あの子も幸せ者です。
lines.en: Thank you. She is a lucky girl.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 由美さんには、留学中に本当にお世話になりました。
lines.en: Yumi helped me so much while I was studying abroad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: こちらこそ、娘と仲良くしていただいて。どうぞ、今日はゆっくり楽しんでいってくださいね。
lines.en: Thank you for being such a good friend to her. Please enjoy yourself today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。お二人の末永いお幸せをお祈りしております。
lines.en: Thank you. I wish the two of them lasting happiness.
lines.stage: Bow again and remain standing until she moves on.

drills.title: Offering condolences
drills.setting: At a wake for a former colleague, Mr. Takagi, you speak briefly with his widow before offering incense.
staging: Keep it short and quiet; letting the end of ご愁傷様でございます trail off is natural. Don't smile.
Avoid repeated words (重ね重ね、たびたび) and direct words for death; say ご逝去 or simply avoid the topic.
Bring 香典 in a black-and-white envelope wrapped in a dark fukusa, and hand it over with both hands.
Bow to the family before and after offering incense, then to the altar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: このたびは、ご愁傷様でございます。
lines.en: Please accept my condolences.
lines.stage: Speak softly; bow deeply and slowly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 本日はお忙しいところ、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you for coming despite your busy schedule.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 高木さんには、会社で大変お世話になりました。
lines.en: Mr. Takagi was so good to me at the company.
lines.stage: Keep your hands together in front.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 主人も、皆さんのことをよく話しておりました。
lines.en: My husband often spoke of all of you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 心よりお悔やみ申し上げます。どうぞ御霊前にお供えください。
lines.en: My deepest sympathy. Please offer this at the altar.
lines.stage: Take the envelope out of the fukusa and hand it over with both hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ご丁寧に、恐れ入ります。
lines.en: Thank you for your kindness.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 何かお手伝いできることがありましたら、おっしゃってください。
lines.en: If there is anything I can do to help, please let me know.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。どうぞ、ご焼香を。
lines.en: Thank you. Please, go ahead and offer incense.
lines.stage: She gestures toward the altar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 失礼いたします。
lines.en: Excuse me.
lines.stage: Bow to the family, walk to the incense burner, bow to the altar.

drills.title: First day at a part-time job
drills.titleJa: アルバイト初日の朝礼
drills.setting: It is your first morning at a café job. The manager, Mr. Okada, holds the morning meeting and asks you to introduce yourself.
staging: Staff stand in a line for 朝礼; step forward one pace to introduce yourself.
今日からお世話になります is the standard opener on a first day; end with よろしくお願いします and a 30-degree bow.
Service phrases are practiced loudly in unison; bow about 45 degrees on ありがとうございました.
Call the manager 店長 and coworkers by family name + さん.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: おはようございます。では、朝礼を始めます。今日から新しい仲間が入りました。自己紹介をお願いします。
lines.en: Good morning. Let's begin the morning meeting. A new member joins us today. Please introduce yourself.
lines.stage: Staff stand in a line facing the manager.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おはようございます。今日からお世話になります、マリア・ロペスです。
lines.en: Good morning. I'm Maria Lopez, and I'm starting today.
lines.stage: Step forward one pace.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 初めてのアルバイトなので、わからないことが多いですが、一生懸命頑張ります。よろしくお願いします。
lines.en: It's my first part-time job, so there's a lot I don't know, but I'll do my best. I look forward to working with you.
lines.stage: Bow about 30 degrees and hold it briefly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: よろしくお願いします。じゃあ、みんなで接客用語を言いましょう。いらっしゃいませ。
lines.en: Welcome aboard. Now, let's all say the service phrases. Irasshaimase.
lines.stage: Everyone repeats loudly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いらっしゃいませ！
lines.en: Welcome!
lines.stage: Smile; slight 15-degree bow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございました。
lines.en: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございました！
lines.en: Thank you very much!
lines.stage: Deeper bow, about 45 degrees.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いいですね。わからないことは、木村さんに聞いてください。
lines.en: Good. Ask Kimura about anything you don't know.
lines.stage: He nods toward a senior coworker.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、わかりました。木村さん、よろしくお願いします。
lines.en: Yes, understood. Kimura, I look forward to working with you.
lines.stage: Turn and bow to Kimura.

drills.title: Working the convenience store register
drills.setting: You play the clerk at a convenience store and use the standard service phrases with a customer.
staging: Store 'manual keigo' uses set phrases such as 〜になります and 〜お預かりします; they are criticized by purists but heard everywhere, so learn to recognize them.
Customers usually reply briefly or just nod; clerks don't expect keigo back.
Say the amount received out loud, then hand the change and receipt with both hands.
Close with a small bow and またお越しくださいませ.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いらっしゃいませ。こんにちは。
lines.en: Welcome. Hello.
lines.stage: Look up and give a small nod.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: これ、お願いします。
lines.en: This, please.
lines.stage: He sets a bento and a drink on the counter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お弁当は温めますか。
lines.en: Would you like the bento heated?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい、お願いします。
lines.en: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: レジ袋はご利用ですか。
lines.en: Would you like a plastic bag?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いえ、大丈夫です。
lines.en: No, I'm fine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お会計、八百六十円になります。
lines.en: Your total comes to 860 yen.
lines.stage: Point to the display.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: じゃあ、千円で。
lines.en: Here's a thousand yen.
lines.stage: He places the bill on the tray.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 千円お預かりします。百四十円のお返しです。ありがとうございました。またお越しくださいませ。
lines.en: Out of a thousand yen. Here's 140 yen change. Thank you very much. Please come again.
lines.stage: Hand the change and receipt with both hands, then bow about 15 degrees.

drills.title: Calling out at a festival stall
drills.setting: At a summer shrine festival you run a takoyaki stall and call to passersby. A customer stops.
staging: Stall talk is loud, casual and friendly: だよ、ね、はいよ; customers may answer casually or politely.
まいど (short for まいどあり) is merchant thanks, especially common in western Japan.
Hand hot food over with both hands and a warning (熱いから気をつけて).
Many festivals ask people to eat near the stall rather than while walking through crowds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いらっしゃい、いらっしゃい！焼きたてのたこ焼きだよ！
lines.en: Step right up! Fresh-made takoyaki!
lines.stage: Call out loudly, turning the balls with a pick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おいしそう！一つください。
lines.en: Looks good! One, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: まいど！ソースとマヨネーズ、かける？
lines.en: Thanks! Sauce and mayo on it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 両方お願いします。
lines.en: Both, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はいよ！青のりは？
lines.en: You got it! Seaweed flakes?
lines.stage: Keep the sauce bottle moving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 青のりはなしで。
lines.en: No seaweed, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい、お待ち！五百円ね。
lines.en: Here you go! Five hundred yen.
lines.stage: Hand over the paper boat with both hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、五百円。
lines.en: Here, five hundred.
lines.stage: She puts a coin in the tray.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ちょうどね。熱いから気をつけて。まいど！
lines.en: Exact change. It's hot, careful. Thanks!
lines.stage: Nod and immediately start calling again.

drills.title: Leaving the office before your boss
drills.setting: Your work is done for the day, but section chief Nomura is still at her desk. You check in with her before leaving.
staging: Ask whether there is anything more to do before you announce you're leaving.
Say お先に失礼します when leaving before others; answer with お疲れ様です, never ご苦労様 (that one goes from seniors to juniors).
Call her 課長 or 野村課長; a title replaces さん.
Push your chair in, give a 15-degree bow toward her desk, and a light bow again at the door. She may speak casually; you stay polite.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 野村課長、今日の資料、机の上に置いておきました。
lines.en: Chief Nomura, I've left today's documents on your desk.
lines.stage: Walk to her desk; don't call across the room.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとう。助かったよ。
lines.en: Thanks. That was a big help.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ほかに何かお手伝いすることはありますか。
lines.en: Is there anything else I can help with?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ううん、大丈夫。今日はもう帰っていいよ。
lines.en: No, it's fine. You can go home for today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、お先に失礼します。
lines.en: Then, excuse me for leaving before you.
lines.stage: Push your chair in and bow about 15 degrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お疲れ様。気をつけて帰ってね。
lines.en: Good work. Get home safe.
lines.stage: She looks up from her screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お疲れ様です。また明日よろしくお願いします。
lines.en: Thank you for your hard work. See you tomorrow.
lines.stage: Light bow again at the door.

drills.title: In the department-store elevator
drills.titleJa: デパートのエレベーターで
drills.setting: An elevator attendant in a department store takes your floor request and helps you find the children's clothing section.
staging: Attendants use formal keigo (まいります、でございます、お申し付けください) and a 15-degree bow at every floor.
A quick 会釈 and ありがとうございました is the right reply; no need to match the keigo.
In elevators, the spot by the buttons is the 'lowest seat': in business settings the junior stands there and holds the door.
Let others step out first with お先にどうぞ when you are nearer the door.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 上へまいります。ご利用の階をお申し付けください。
lines.en: Going up. Please tell me which floor you need.
lines.stage: She bows about 15 degrees at the doors.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 五階をお願いします。
lines.en: Fifth floor, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 五階でございますね。かしこまりました。
lines.en: The fifth floor. Certainly.
lines.stage: She presses the button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、子供服は五階でしょうか。
lines.en: Excuse me, is children's clothing on five?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 子供服は六階でございます。五階は紳士服の売り場でございます。
lines.en: Children's clothing is on six. The fifth floor is menswear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、じゃあ六階でお願いします。
lines.en: Oh, then sixth floor, please.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 承知いたしました。六階でございます。お足元にお気をつけくださいませ。
lines.en: Certainly. Sixth floor. Please watch your step.
lines.stage: She holds the door with one hand and bows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございました。お先にどうぞ。
lines.en: Thank you. After you.
lines.stage: Quick nod to her; gesture for the person beside you to go first.

drills.title: Thanking your homeroom teacher at graduation
drills.titleJa: 卒業式で担任の先生にお礼
drills.setting: After the high school graduation ceremony, you find your homeroom teacher, Mr. Fujii, in the schoolyard.
staging: Graduation is the moment for a student's deepest thank-you bow to a teacher: about 45 degrees, held.
お世話になりました (past) marks the end of a period in a relationship.
The teacher often talks casually (〜ね、〜よ) to students; the student stays polite and uses 〜てくださる for the teacher's kindness.
Hand the class gift or message card with both hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 藤井先生、三年間、本当にお世話になりました。
lines.en: Mr. Fujii, thank you so much for these three years.
lines.stage: Holding your diploma tube, bow deeply and hold it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 卒業おめでとう。よく頑張ったね。
lines.en: Congratulations on graduating. You worked hard.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 日本に来たばかりのころ、先生が毎日声をかけてくださって、心強かったです。
lines.en: When I'd just come to Japan, you spoke to me every day, and it gave me courage.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうか。あのころは、日本語で話すのも大変だったよね。
lines.en: I see. Back then, even talking in Japanese was hard for you, wasn't it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。先生のおかげで、大学に合格できました。
lines.en: Yes. Thanks to you, I got into university.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それは君の努力の結果だよ。大学でも頑張って。
lines.en: That's the result of your own effort. Keep it up at university.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。これ、クラスのみんなからです。
lines.en: Thank you. This is from everyone in the class.
lines.stage: Hand over the message album with both hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとう。大切にするよ。
lines.en: Thank you. I'll treasure it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: また学校に遊びに来ます。先生もお元気で。
lines.en: I'll come back to visit the school. Please take care.
lines.stage: Final bow before walking away.

drills.title: Sharing a hanami spot
drills.titleJa: 花見の場所をゆずり合う
drills.setting: Your group has a tarp under the cherry trees. A woman from another group asks if the space next to you is free.
staging: Groups often claim spots early with a tarp; ask before sitting next to someone.
Shoes come off before stepping on a tarp.
Sharing snacks with neighboring groups is common; accept with thanks and offer something back.
Take all your trash home and leave the spot clean.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、この辺り、空いていますか。
lines.en: Excuse me, is this area free?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい、どうぞ。こちら、少し詰めますね。
lines.en: Yes, go ahead. We'll squeeze over a bit.
lines.stage: Pull your tarp in and smile.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。助かります。
lines.en: Thank you. That helps a lot.
lines.stage: She bows slightly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いえいえ。今日はいい天気ですね。桜も満開ですし。
lines.en: Not at all. Lovely weather today, and the cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 本当ですね。よかったら、これ、どうぞ。お団子です。
lines.en: It really is. Please have some if you like. They're dumplings.
lines.stage: She holds out a pack.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: えっ、いいんですか。じゃあ、遠慮なくいただきます。うちのお菓子もどうぞ。
lines.en: Oh, really? Then I'll gladly have some. Please have some of our snacks too.
lines.stage: Take one with both hands, then offer your bag of snacks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。何時ごろまでいらっしゃいますか。
lines.en: Thank you. Until about what time will you be here?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 夕方には片付けて帰ります。ゴミは全部持って帰りますので。
lines.en: We'll tidy up and leave by evening. We'll take all our trash home.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 私たちもです。お互い楽しみましょう。
lines.en: So will we. Let's both enjoy it.

drills.title: Seeing off a guest
drills.setting: Your guest, Mr. Okawa, is getting ready to leave after dinner at your home. You see him off at the door.
staging: Stand when the guest stands, and walk ahead to the genkan to set out their shoes.
何のお構いもしませんで is the set humble phrase: 'I did nothing for you', said even after a big dinner.
See the guest past the door: to the gate, the elevator, or until they are out of sight, and bow again if they turn around.
Don't shut the door or switch off the porch light the moment they step out; it feels like shooing them away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そろそろ失礼します。長居してしまって、すみません。
lines.en: I'd better be going. Sorry for staying so long.
lines.stage: He begins to rise.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いいえ、何のお構いもしませんで。
lines.en: Not at all. I'm afraid I didn't do much for you.
lines.stage: Stand up with him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: とんでもない。すっかりご馳走になりました。
lines.en: Not at all. It was a wonderful meal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お荷物、お持ちしますね。玄関までお送りします。
lines.en: Let me carry your bag. I'll see you to the door.
lines.stage: Walk ahead of him to the genkan.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you.
lines.stage: He sits on the step to put on his shoes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 靴べらをどうぞ。足元にお気をつけください。
lines.en: Here's a shoehorn. Please watch your step.
lines.stage: Hold out the shoehorn by its end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 今日は本当に楽しかったです。今度はぜひうちにも来てください。
lines.en: I had a wonderful time today. Next time, please come to our place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。ぜひ伺います。お気をつけてお帰りください。
lines.en: Thank you, I'd love to. Have a safe trip home.
lines.stage: Step outside with him; bow about 30 degrees.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、失礼します。
lines.en: Well then, goodbye.
lines.stage: He bows and walks off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: またいらしてください。
lines.en: Please come again.
lines.stage: Stay at the gate until he is out of sight; bow again if he looks back.
